rationale: C21 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are letters to the Speaker urging House action during the current session on legislation already passed by the Senate with bipartisan support. They share a close rhetorical sequence: an opening expression of hope for favorable House action, explanation of the proposal's importance and federal/local implications, reference to prior presidential recommendations, notice of bipartisan Senate passage, and a closing hope for prompt House passage. C10 is also a closely timed legislative-advocacy letter to the same Speaker, but its claim-by-claim rebuttal structure is substantially different. C20 shares congressional advocacy language but is less closely matched in recipient, sequence, and machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am writing to you to express my hope that the House will complete legislative action on a home rule bill ... before this session of the 81st Congress adjourns.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to express my earnest hope that the House of Representatives will take favorable action at this session upon legislation providing Federal aid for elementary and secondary schools.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively close opening formulation urging the Speaker to secure House action on specified legislation during the current session.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In my Message to Congress transmitting the Budget for the fiscal year 1947, I said...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It will be recalled that ... I included in the Budget for the fiscal year 1949 an estimate ... to cover the cost of such legislation.
shared_material.explanation: Both support the present request by invoking an earlier presidential recommendation made through a budget message.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The bill which passed the Senate unanimously, received the support of both Republican and Democratic members of that body.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A bill to provide Federal aid to education has recently been passed in the Senate by a substantial majority of both parties.
shared_material.explanation: Parallel penultimate appeal based on prior bipartisan Senate passage.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hope that the House will not adjourn this session without completing action on this important measure.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope that legislation for this purpose will soon be passed also by the House of Representatives.
shared_material.explanation: Closely parallel closing request for House passage, completing the same operative rhetorical sequence.
